text: The authors state that, mirroring the mostly null results of Parrish et al. (2022) for single-turn arguments, adding counter-arguments does not improve human crowdworkers' accuracy on hard multiple-choice reading comprehension questions with time-limited passage access, compared with an argument-free baseline. With weak abstention incentives accuracy gets slightly worse, and with strong incentives there is no effect.
title: Two-turn counter-arguments also fail to help, mirroring Parrish et al.'s single-turn null result
